why: A garden-centre chain selling 200,000 bags of compost a year at $6.00, bought at $4.00 to $4.20 with $1.70 of handling, is believable.
5,650 business software accounts, a $240 hosting fee and support plans costing hundreds to a few thousand dollars a year are consistent with the stated $3.38 million and believable.
600,000 new subscribers with first-year margins of $1.50 to $31.50 on 90-day spend of $58 to $298 is believable for a recipe-box company.
A fitness chain selling 300,000 shakes a year at $4.00, bought at $2.00 to $2.40 with $1.40 of other costs, is believable.
Line revenues of $1 to $29 million (about $113 million in all) against 6 to 58 engineers per line, roughly $400,000 per engineer, are believable for a loss-making device maker.
Hand filleting at 10 kg an hour, a machine at 30 kg an hour costing about $19,000 over three years and an $18 wage are believable, and 306 days fits six days a week.
Both pies sum to 100%, and 5,400 summer exit interviews is believable for a rural farm museum.
A software reseller's executive on a retainer plus 4% renewal and 25% new-business commission, working 8.5 hours a day, 5 days a week, 48 weeks a year, is believable.
Product revenues of EUR 58 to 153 million with margins of 6% to 15% and modest growth are believable for a bicycle maker.
Each unit's efficiency and fuel-switching cuts add to its stated total (42, 37, 30, 65, 27 thousand tonnes), believable decade-long cuts for a steel mill emitting millions of tonnes a year.
